full_judgment: Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, strenuously submits that the learned appellate Court on consideration of the evidence on record came to the conclusion that the plaintiff as well as the defendant has possessed the suit land jointly. Relying upon the evidence of PW 9, he submits that the witnesses of the plaintiff admitted the possession of the defendant in the suit land. I have gone through the judgment of the last court of fact. It appears that it, on consideration of the evidence, held that then plaintiff and the defendant have possessed the suit land. Although the plaintiff claimed that he is the real owner of the suit land and in exclusive possession of the same but such claim had not been proved. As the defendant has also possessed the suit land so the instant suit for simple declaration is not maintainable without the prayer for recovery of khas possession. One of the important criteria of a benami transaction, that is possession, is found in favour of the defendant.
